name: Gwern

attributes.attribute: Child of princess Branwen and king Matholwch.
Named king of Ireland in his infancy.
Killed Gwern by burning him alive at age three.
His death provoked the great battle in which most Welsh heroes died.

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gwern was the young son of the Welsh princess Branwen and king Matholwch of Ireland. His uncle Efnisien mutilated the king's horses, so Matholwch held Branwen prisoner in Ireland. There she bore Gwern, named king in infancy. When Gwern turned three, Efnisien killed him by burning him alive. The act sparked the great battle in which most Welsh heroes and all warriors of Ireland died.

okr.objective: Detail the short life of Gwern and the battle his death sparked.
key_results: Gwern was the child of Branwen and Matholwch
Efnisien's mutilation of the horses led to Branwen's imprisonment
Gwern was named king in infancy
Efnisien burned Gwern alive, causing the great battle
